answer: A sybil farm should die at the garden gate, not the ballot. Let each resident extend exactly three permanent invitations, ever, and any admitted newcomer's later misconduct retires the inviter's remaining slots. To seat ten thousand clones you need thousands of real accounts willing to spend that one-time slot, and each spent slot destroys something the farm cannot mint: a bounded-degree graph. Cost rises with the square of the intended size, since every new node needs edges only honest residents hold. Inside the kernel of any hollow cluster, that edge budget runs out.
